title: Preserve git's original file state when conflict detection is uncertain or git errors
context: Two reproducible data-loss bugs: (1) the conflict regex failed silently on EMPTY hunks and CRLF systems, leaving markers while reporting success; (2) git's binary-file errors (exit 255) were treated as resolved output, truncating files to zero bytes.
decision: Introduced a write=null sentinel: when git's exit status indicates error (outside 1-127 range) or when any conflict marker survives the resolution pass, return write=null and conflict=true, forcing the CLI to exit 1 and write nothing, leaving the file exactly as git populated it.
consequences: Unrecognized conflicts and git-level errors now fail safely instead of silently corrupting the file
The driver's contract is explicit: write=null means 'I couldn't safely handle this, human must resolve'
Callers must handle the null case, preventing accidental data loss from coercing to empty string
Binary files, CRLF systems, and future unrecognized hunk shapes all degrade gracefully
alternatives_rejected: Continue treating all errors as resolved output by coercing to empty string (silent truncation)
Attempt to reconstruct or guess at merged content when detection fails (more guessing, more risk)
Leave the marker-survival defense out and rely only on regex strictness (regression risk)
